sections.summary: Split the GitHub markdown pipeline behind a lazy boundary and named the vendor chunks. The plan's premise had drifted: ReviewComments.tsx does not import GitHubMarkdownContent — the real call sites are MarkdownFilePreview.tsx (DiffSurface) and RemoteReviewThreads.tsx / PullRequestContext.tsx (MultiFileReview), none of them owned. So the boundary went inside GitHubMarkdownContent.tsx itself: it is now `lazy(() => import('./GitHubMarkdownRenderer'))` under Suspense with an exported GitHubMarkdownFallback that renders the raw source in a `<pre>` inside the identical wrapper, which gives every consumer laziness with no non-owned source edit. Pure helpers moved to a new githubMarkdown.ts; the heavy react-markdown/remark/rehype/parse5 code moved to GitHubMarkdownRenderer.tsx. Added `manualChunks` (vendor-react, vendor-diffs, vendor-markdown, vendor-shiki) with an exclusion for on-demand shiki grammars/themes. vendor-markdown (314,958 B) now has exactly one static importer: the lazy GitHubMarkdownRenderer chunk, and no markdown package appears in any pre-mount chunk.

sections.deviations: Three, all measured rather than assumed. (1) The plan's vendor-markdown pattern included `hast-*` and `entities`; applied verbatim it made things WORSE (pre-mount 1,971,591 B) because shiki's HTML serializer shares hast-util-to-html / property-information / hastscript / stringify-entities, which turns vendor-markdown into a static dependency of vendor-shiki and vendor-diffs. Narrowed the pattern to markdown-only packages; a comment in the config records why. (2) The plan's vendor-shiki pattern folded all 11 MB of @shikijs/langs into one 8.2 MB chunk; added an ON_DEMAND_HIGHLIGHT_ASSETS exclusion for @shikijs/langs, @shikijs/themes, @pierre/theme and shiki/dist/langs. (3) The plan expected >= 240 KB off the closure; measured -164 KB, because roughly 90 KB of hast/property-information/entity tables is genuinely shared with the shiki highlighter that is already on the pre-mount path (P31 owns shiki). Also: three consumer dom tests were edited outside the literal ownership list — see blockers/reviewNotes.

sections.summary: firstTreePath is now local and @pierre/trees left the boot chunk. New treePathOrder.ts carries compareTreePaths + firstTreePath, a faithful port of the library's path-store sort (directories before files per depth, case-insensitive natural digit-aware segment compare, byte order tie-break); firstTreePath is a single min-scan rather than a sort. New treeWidgetOrder.ts holds orderPathsForTree as the only remaining @pierre/trees importer. treeExpansion.ts re-exports both, which is what keeps workspaceMode.ts, Explorer.tsx and the explicitly-forbidden RepositoryWorkspace.tsx unchanged — Rollup traces the re-export and no path-store source remains in the boot chunk.

sections.deviations: Env var is HORUS_GIT_SHIM_LOG per the track brief rather than the plan's $HORUS_GIT_LOG. The shim is zsh, not bash: it reads zsh's in-process $EPOCHREALTIME because a date/python3 subprocess per spawn would cost more than most commands being measured (BSD date has no %N and macOS bash is 3.2); `git` and `gh` are symlinks to one script so no wrapper process sits in front of the measurement. reviewNotes:
Look at these first.

1. REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED, worth re-checking. P09's `manualChunks` made Rollup fold Vite's `preload-helper` into `vendor-shiki`, so the entry chunk statically imported 206 KB of highlighter and index.html carried a modulepreload for it — 206 KB fetched and evaluated before boot even started. Fixed in electron.vite.config.ts by mapping `vite/preload-helper` to its own `vite-preload` manual chunk (manual chunks are never merged by Rollup's small-chunk merging). The scary part is that the pre-mount total barely moved when it happened, so I added `MAX_ENTRY_CLOSURE_BYTES = 64 KB` on the entry's own static closure to check:entry; it is 2,940 B now. This budget was not in the plan — remove it if you disagree.

2. The two manualChunks patterns in the plan are wrong as written and I changed both, with measurements in the progress log. `hast-*`/`entities` in vendor-markdown pushed the pre-mount closure UP to 1,971,591 B because shiki shares those packages; `shiki|@shikijs/*` without an exclusion produced a single 8.2 MB chunk containing every grammar. Both comments explaining this live in electron.vite.config.ts.

3. Design decision to sanity-check: GitHubMarkdownContent.tsx is now the lazy boundary itself rather than each call site being wrapped. This was the only way to get laziness to MarkdownFilePreview, RemoteReviewThreads and PullRequestContext without editing non-owned source. The visible consequence is that a pull request body / review comment / markdown preview shows its raw source in a `<pre>` for the frame or two the chunk takes to arrive. The `<pre>` carries four inline style properties (margin, font-family, font-size inherit, pre-wrap, break-word) because styles.css is not owned; if you would rather it be a class, that is a one-line CSS rule plus dropping RAW_MARKDOWN_STYLE.

4. treePathOrder.ts is a hand port of @pierre/trees' internal sort. I pinned it with an exact-equality test against `prepareFileTreeInput` on 200 mixed paths, 12 rotations of that fixture, and a full-sort comparison — but it is a port of an internal, unversioned implementation, so a @pierre/trees upgrade could drift it silently. The test would catch that.

5. I could not verify the probes end to end: running them launches Horus.app, which this track is forbidden to do. They are syntax-checked, cdp.mjs imports without side effects, and the pure helpers (markKey, startupMarks, median, round, appendResult, and the whole closure walker) are unit tested. The git shim WAS exercised by hand — 4 spawns logged with correct exit-status passthrough and transparent pass-through when HORUS_GIT_SHIM_LOG is unset. Someone should run `bun run perf:startup-probe after` once against a fresh `bun run update:mac` before trusting the numbers.

6. `palette.workspaceRenders` in the startup probe reads `window.__horusMetrics?.workspaceRenders` and reports null until Track C's P15 exposes it. That is deliberate — a wrong zero would look like a passing target.

7. P08 removed the awaits but I did not add a fallback gate, because App.tsx already renders CachedWorkspaceFallback (a real 120-row tree) while the WorkspaceRoot module store is empty. If the fallback visibly flashes on a warm machine, the plan's 60 ms timer inside App is the follow-up and it belongs to whoever owns App.tsx.

8. The P11 change means the titlebar memory readout shows '—' until someone opens the HUD once. The plan asked for this ("not before the popover has been opened once") but it is the one user-visible behaviour change in this track.
